claim: More facts attached to one cue slows recognition and lowers accuracy in people. Shown with fictional facts, real knowledge and similar-concept Dutch materials; accuracy cost is mostly extra false alarms.
agent_test: Build a note library with N=1,2,4,8 notes per entity. Query by entity. Compare accuracy and false accepts at equal prompt tokens (pad low-N arms with unrelated notes).

claim: The cost per extra item is roughly logarithmic in the number of items per cue (ACT-R S = S0 - ln fan). In one preprint, humans scored 91.2, 82.4, 71.8 percent at fan 1, 2, 4 and log beat power law (BIC > 15). The first extra item hurts most. Indirect support (gap search): in a long-context test, the first 10 percent of hard distractors caused 58 percent of the total loss for one 7B model (linear would be 10 percent), a convex curve like the log shape.
agent_test: Measure agent accuracy at 1,2,4,8,16 notes per cue; fit log vs power; check the slope per doubling. Only Guo et al. compare forms directly, and that preprint has provenance doubts.

claim: LLMs show a fan effect when all facts are in context, but it is small at fan 2 on recognition (accuracy 0.991 to 0.915; d-prime about 4.1 to 3.1 for GPT-4) and appears in token probability only in some models (Mistral, SOLAR; not GPT-2, Llama-2).
agent_test: Run the fan paradigm on the exact model the agent uses at fan 1,2,4,8; record probability of 'absent'. Do not assume the effect transfers across models.

claim: In LLMs, accuracy of reading the latest value of a key falls log-linearly with the number of earlier values for that key (3 to 400 updates), across 35 to 39 models, from different labs.
agent_test: Overwrite test on the agent memory: same key updated k times (k=1..100), query latest. Compare append-only vs replace-in-code at equal tokens.

claim: The harm is the number of competing items for one cue, not input length: tracking more keys at fixed length, or asking about fewer keys in a fixed input, gives the same log-linear drop. Context window size does not predict resistance (t=-0.14, p=.886).
agent_test: Hold total tokens constant; vary items per cue vs filler tokens. Expect items per cue to matter and filler not to.

claim: Telling the model to forget, ignore or focus on later values barely helps (under 10 points; directed forgetting +1 point). Chain of thought did not help retrieval.
agent_test: At equal tokens compare an 'ignore old notes' prompt vs code that removes superseded notes. Expect code removal to win.

claim: A structural reset in the context (a mock question-answer turn before the query) gave a large gain; Gemini Flash 2.0 at 150 updates matched baseline at 30-45 updates. Accuracy still fell with update count.
agent_test: Test inserting a turn boundary before the query vs none, on stale-value retrieval, same token budget.

claim: Near-miss competitors under the same cue hurt most. Hard distractors cut Llama2 accuracy from 0.5642 to 0.4733 (1 distractor, far) and 0.3106 (8); same-slot conflicts cut agent memory uptake more than unrelated memories; a literal-overlap distractor cut GPT-4o effective length to 1K.
agent_test: Add 4 near-duplicates vs 4 unrelated notes to the candidate set; compare accuracy. Add a code-side near-duplicate merge step and compare.

claim: Unrelated extra items cost little: random passages beside the gold did not hurt Llama2 (0.5642 to 0.5859 at 14, small and partly non-significant); unrelated memories moved lexical plasticity by -0.02. But dense retrieval lost 0.18 with unrelated memories, and MPT and Falcon behaved differently.
agent_test: Vary load type (unrelated vs related) and retriever type (lexical vs dense) in the agent; check whether unrelated load is free for the retrieval path actually used.

claim: Competitor similarity matters as much as count. False alarms at high similarity were 23.1 percent for humans and 41.3 percent for dense passage retrieval; similar concepts still show fan in Dutch; interference raises familiarity so false alarms rise even when hits do not.
agent_test: Track false accepts separately from misses. Test whether a recall-to-reject verification (compare the whole fact) lowers false accepts at equal tokens.

claim: A foil that shares a cue with a stored fact is accepted more often (King and Anderson: connected foils much slower and more errors). Shared-cue near matches produce a spurious intersection.
agent_test: Verify the chosen note against the whole claim, not one shared key; compare false-accept rate with and without a full-match check.

claim: Strengthening one item protects it from a crowded cue: relative strength, not count, sets retrieval; practice (about 600 trials per sentence) removed the fan effect (same asymptote 0.36 s). No LLM list-strength effect was found.
agent_test: Test pinning or repeating the key note vs equal weight among N notes, at equal tokens. LLM test only partly analogous.

claim: Integrating facts into one coherent model or theme removes the fan cost on the shared dimension (young adults single-location 1395, 1448, 1415 ms vs multiple-location 1441, 1615, 1853 ms). ACT-R and Radvansky disagree on why, and a Chinese replication with changed materials differed (snippet only).
agent_test: Store N related facts as one integrated case note vs N loose notes; compare retrieval accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Attention on a cue increases the fan cost of that cue (focused slope 98 vs 63 ms; 118 vs 73 ms), the opposite of the mental-model prediction. One lab (CMU), small samples.
agent_test: Give the query extra weight on one cue (tag order or emphasis) and see whether crowded-cue cost rises or falls.

claim: Items placed in the middle of many retrieved items are recovered worse (about 20 points; GPT-3.5 75.8 percent at index 0, 53.8 at index 9, 63.2 at index 19). Gold nearest the query is best with 18 distractors (0.378 vs 0.235 far vs 0.180 mid).
agent_test: Order candidate notes by score with the best last, vs random order, at equal tokens.

claim: In LLMs, proactive interference (latest value after many updates) is far worse than retroactive (earliest value): Cohen d=1.73 across 39 models; earliest-state accuracy stays near 98-100 percent while latest-state collapses. The reverse of the usual human pattern.
agent_test: Test recall of first vs latest value in agent memory; if old values stay near ceiling, keep a replace policy rather than versions.

claim: Whether parameter size predicts resistance to proactive interference is disputed: Wang and Sun find size class predicts it (t=3.03, p=.005, N=30); Chattaraj and Raj find R2 = 0.06 (p=.14) for PI but 0.49 for retroactive.
agent_test: Measure the PI slope on the agent's own model and any cheaper model; do not assume a larger model fixes it.

claim: Writing new facts to an old cue harms retrieval of the old facts (Lewis and Anderson); in agent memory, repeated history and same-slot conflicts cut update uptake (-0.32, -0.48 vs unrelated, lexical, count 8).
agent_test: Measure retrieval of old notes before and after adding a conflicting note for the same cue; add a supersede-in-code write rule and compare.

claim: Prefiltering the candidate set per query lifts selection: tool choice 13.62 percent with all descriptions, 43.13 percent with top-1 vector retrieval, 18.20 percent with a keyword prefilter (one model, 20 trials). Gap search: top-k depth effects depend on the reader (see K27), so one sweep on the deployed model is needed.
agent_test: Compare passing the full library vs top-k filtered by code at equal tokens; sweep k.

claim: Active context management helps modestly zero-shot: Claude-4-Sonnet +5.90 and GPT-4.1 +6.58 on PI-LLM, DeepSeek-V3 -0.12, and tool use hurt short contexts (99.13 to 90.43); the large gains needed RL training of a 13B model. Gap search: a model-written bounded memory lost 15 points to full context on gpt-5.4 (92 to 77 percent, LongMemEval knowledge update, n=78).
agent_test: Add a fold/forget tool to the agent and test at equal tokens on long runs only; check it does not hurt short runs.

claim: Fan-division in retrieval (activation divided by out-degree) helps agent memory: SYNAPSE weighted F1 40.5 vs 33.3, and removing fan cut open-domain F1 from 25.9 to 16.8, at 814 vs 16,910 tokens per query.
agent_test: Add fan-normalized scoring to the library lookup; ablate it.

claim: Model uncertainty about cue overload rarely appears in output: fan shows in token probabilities when the item is absent, and only 8.6 percent of PI failures contain an explicit refusal (0 percent under RI). The model usually answers with a stale value.
agent_test: Do not use the model's own 'I am unsure' as a trigger. Log token probability of the answer for crowded cues and compare with correctness.

claim: 4-bit quantization worsens PI under semantically similar overwrites (Qwen 81.0 to 68.3 percent; p<=2.6e-6) but not for numeric attributes.
agent_test: Only relevant if the agent runs a quantized model; then re-measure its fan slope.

claim: Memory agents mostly add and rarely delete or update (insert in 76.8 percent of operations), and full systems score low when interference is deep (best average 33.4 percent).
agent_test: Count delete and update operations in the agent's memory log; require supersede-on-conflict.

claim: Selecting memories by their effect on the answer beats similarity: top-3 similar memories are often stale or misleading; vector and reflection memory adopt poisoned memories (task score 0.846 vs 0.845 but bad-memory rejection 0.990).
agent_test: Compare similarity-ranked top-k to a swap-in/out test on the answer, at equal tokens.

claim: Recency alone does not stop an agent accepting an invalid older memory (poison acceptance .02 lexical, .00 dense), but persistent-update or authoritative wording raised acceptance to .23/.12 and .26/.14.
agent_test: Test how memory write wording changes later adoption; use plain, code-set supersede flags.

claim: The best top-k depends on the reader model. Some readers plateau near k=10 (FLAN-T5, GPT-3.5); others peak below k=5 and then decline, sometimes under their no-retrieval score (Llama, Claude-3-haiku). With a strong retriever, quality rises then falls (inverted U). The strongest 2024 models (o1, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) kept improving to about 100k tokens. No current-frontier sweep from k=1 to 20 was found.
agent_test: Sweep k=1,3,5,10,20 on the deployed model with the real library, near-duplicates left in, at each k; pick k at the knee; check the spread near the peak (RAGGED stability).

claim: Dedupe or diversity reranking of the top-k hurts on clean pools (-0.7 to -33.0 S-Recall points on HotpotQA; MMR costs 3.1 EM) and pays only when the pool is measurably redundant and the task needs several distinct pieces (+13.6 to +24.1 S-Recall at heavy redundancy). A rule that fires only when top-k has fewer distinct documents than the query needs captures most of the gain.
agent_test: Measure the near-duplicate pair fraction of the library (cosine above 0.95). Compare plain top-k, always-dedupe and dedupe-when-redundant on single-note lookup and multi-note questions at equal tokens.

claim: Decoupling history into small units, grouping them, and retrieving groups first then raw text only if needed beat flat top-20 with fewer tokens (Qwen3-8B on LoCoMo: F1 43.98 vs 36.48 at 4,711 vs 8,633 tokens; GPT-5 nano 50.00 vs 48.17 for the next best system at 6,581 vs 9,155). A group cap of 12 components (average 4.5) beat 8, 10 and 14. Whole pipeline changed at once, so grouping alone is not isolated.
agent_test: Same notes, three layouts at equal tokens: flat, grouped under sub-cues with group cap 4 to 12, integrated case notes. Query by cue. Compare accuracy and false accepts, with N from 2 to 50 per cue.

claim: A code-side supersede rule is exact only when cues are canonical. Deterministic stores scored 100 percent on temporal qualifiers and 92 percent on chained supersession, but 5 percent on obfuscated identifiers and 0 percent on cross-lingual cues. An LLM at write time or in a mutation hook lifted the 345-case score from 70 to 93 percent at about 17 cents per 385 cases and 2.3 s per case. Accuracy at equal tokens was not measured.
agent_test: Give each note a canonical cue key and a supersede flag set in code at write time; use one model call only to normalise the cue. Compare with append-only at equal tokens on update questions.

claim: Whether a one-live-value-per-cue write rule beats an append-only library is open and mixed. Zep, Cognee and MemoryOS with update or invalidation scored 35.6 to 44.4 substring EM on LongMemEval knowledge update against 20.0 for long context and embedding RAG. But a model-written bounded memory lost 15 points to full context (gpt-5.4, 92 to 77 percent), and a vendor reports gains from moving to add-only. None of these is a code rule at equal tokens.
agent_test: Three arms at equal prompt tokens in a real agent loop: append-only, code-replace per canonical cue, model-merge. Count setup tokens and calls (G7). Score latest-value accuracy and false accepts.

claim: Answer-token entropy can gate a second lookup on open readers: expansion only when entropy is high gave +1.42 BLEU and +1.78 F1 with 679 fewer tokens (Qwen3-8B, LoCoMo); simple uncertainty estimators matched complex adaptive-retrieval pipelines with under one retrieval call per question (LLaMA 3.1-8B). Both fall short of an oracle trigger. Closed models that hide logits needed a proxy model. Not tested on crowded cues.
agent_test: On the deployed model (if it exposes logprobs), log answer entropy for cues with N=1..16 notes; check ROC-AUC against correctness; then test a second lookup when entropy passes a threshold, at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning mode and size do not clearly lower the proactive-interference slope. Reasoning models do better on retroactive interference (RIES 178.0 vs 150.3) but o1 ranked 35 of 39 on the proactive score (PIES 22.0); Wang and Sun left reasoning models out. Templated updates are solved by frontier models with full history in context (100 percent), but model-written notes still lost to full history on real updates (gpt-5.4 low reasoning 77 vs 92 percent).
agent_test: Run the key-overwrite test (k=1..100 updates) on the deployed model with reasoning off and on, and at full precision vs quantized; compare slopes per doubling.

claim: Repeating the whole prompt twice raised accuracy for 7 non-reasoning models (47 of 70 combinations better, none worse; NameIndex 21.33 to 97.33 percent for one model); padding to equal length did not help; with reasoning on it was neutral. This is only an indirect hint that re-exposing the key note near the query could help; there is no LLM test that practice or past successful use makes a note safer from crowding.
agent_test: List the chosen note a second time next to the query, vs once, at equal tokens, with N=8 competitors. Separately, test a use-count score that boosts notes that were used successfully before.
